correctness.rationale: The exact derivative identity for two coeval unit-power kernels is reconstructed, including normalization and endpoint limits; optimizing its sign over all positive amplitude weights gives the discriminant boundary R_c=17+12√2. The derivative numerator in normalized time is quartic with all but possibly its quadratic coefficient positive, so Descartes bounds positive roots by two, proving the witness has exactly two strict extrema. The exact witness has E(10)=1/2 and E′(10)=−41/4840. Independent-expression finite checks passed; they are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Distinct aftershock onset/regularization scales are motivated in seismological prior work. The theorem completely resolves a natural minimal two-component mechanism: under approximately 34-fold scale separation no amplitude variation can mimic a rise–fall–rise apparent exponent, while larger contrast permits one and never more than two reversals. This supplies an exact structural diagnostic with a rational example, without asserting data-level detectability or practical hazard conclusions.
